Planning a trip to Xilitla with kids raises more questions than answers: Will they be allowed into Las Pozas? Are there activities suited to their age? How do you get there without hassle? Visiting Xilitla with kids is completely doable, but it takes specific information that few sources offer with real, up-to-date details.

This guide is for traveling with kids. If you're traveling without them, the general guide is things to do in Xilitla, and the town's practical info—how to get there and what to pack—is on our Xilitla page.

In this guide you'll find everything you need to organize your visit: exact hours, 2026 prices, which activities suit each age and how to choose among the available family tours. A key fact: at the Edward James Sculpture Garden (Las Pozas), kids under 6 get in free, and children ages 6 to 12 pay $120 MXN at the ticket office.

At huasteca-potosina.com we work with local guides and operators across the region. This guide is updated with the real experiences of people who travel the Huasteca Potosina every week. When you're ready, book your guided tour in the Huasteca Potosina.

The best things to do in Xilitla with kids: what to visit and how

Edward James's Las Pozas: the surrealist walk little ones love

The Edward James Sculpture Garden, known as Las Pozas, is the centerpiece when you plan Xilitla with kids. Admission is $180 MXN per adult and $120 MXN for children ages 6 to 12; kids under 6 get in free. For now there are no online sales: you reserve your time slot for free in the official system (up to 60 days ahead) and pay at the garden's ticket office on the day of your visit, in cash or by card. The garden is open Wednesday to Monday, 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., with last entry at 4:00 p.m.; it's closed on Tuesdays. You must pay an extra $30 MXN for a Spanish-speaking guide, no exceptions.

Family groups arrive before 10:00 a.m. to see the sculptures with fewer people around and enjoy the morning light on the natural pools. Book your Xilitla tour with kids with a local guide included for a safer, richer experience.

The Magic Town of Xilitla: streets, coffee and Huastec culture

Beyond Las Pozas, downtown Xilitla makes for a family-friendly walk: the local market, the parish church and the natural lookouts can all be covered on foot in under two hours. The mild climate makes walking with kids comfortable in the morning.

If you'd like to work food into your outing, see our guide to restaurants in Xilitla, where you'll find options for the whole family, including regional dishes that kids usually take to easily.

Tips before visiting Xilitla with kids: what to bring and how to prepare

Planning a trip to Xilitla with kids means paying attention to details that make the difference between a comfortable outing and an exhausting one.

  • Stick to your time slot: at Las Pozas, if you're late, you lose your slot. Arrive at least 15 minutes early.
  • Reserve your time slot online: reserving in the official system is free, and admission is paid at the ticket office on the day of your visit. If you see $170 MXN on other websites, that was the online price in early 2026. See our complete article on Las Pozas for the reservation steps.
  • Choose the best time to visit: November to March are the most recommended months for families. Check our guide to the best time to visit the Huasteca Potosina before you confirm your dates.
  • Essential gear: Bring closed-toe, non-slip shoes, a change of clothes for the kids, insect repellent and sunscreen.

Frequently asked questions about Xilitla with kids

From what age can children go into Las Pozas in Xilitla?

There's no need to wait until they're 6: kids under 6 get in free, and children ages 6 to 12 pay $120 MXN in 2026. Admission is paid at the garden's ticket office on the day of your visit, after you reserve your time slot for free in the official system.

How much does it cost to visit Xilitla with kids in 2026?

Admission to Las Pozas is $180 MXN for adults and $120 MXN for children (ages 6–12) at the ticket office, plus $30 MXN for a Spanish-speaking guide, which is mandatory. Our packages with a hotel in Xilitla, 3 to 5 days long, range from $8,699 MXN to $16,500 MXN per couple; for families, we put together a custom quote.

How do you get to Xilitla from Ciudad Valles?

Xilitla is 1 h 30 min from Ciudad Valles by road. You can drive yourself or take family tours that include transportation from Ciudad Valles, with stops at the main sights of the Huasteca Potosina.

Is it safe to travel to Xilitla with young children?

Yes, Xilitla is a safe destination for families. We recommend booking family tours with certified local guides, sticking to Las Pozas' schedule and wearing proper shoes for the trails. For kids under 6, the town and its lookouts are a more comfortable choice than the hiking routes.
